title: Professional Writing Skills
description: Develop the writing skills required in professional and academic environments: formal emails, business reports, executive summaries, academic essays, and application documents. This course is aimed at B1 completers who work or study in English-speaking contexts and need to produce clear, well-structured, and appropriately formal written documents.

lessons.title: Register, Tone, and Style in Professional English

content.content: {"time":1700000011000,"blocks":[{"id":"aB1cD2eF3g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Register refers to the level of formality appropriate to a particular context. In professional English, register is determined by the relationship between writer and reader, the purpose of the communication, and the genre (email, report, essay, etc.)."}},{"id":"hI4jK5lM6n","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Formal professional writing is characterised by: impersonal tone (avoiding I think in favour of It is argued that...), precise vocabulary (avoiding vague words like thing, stuff, a lot), complete sentences (no fragments or contractions), and passive constructions where the agent is less important than the action."}},{"id":"oP7qR8sT9u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Contrast these pairs: I need you to fix this ASAP (informal) vs. I would be grateful if you could address this matter at your earliest convenience (formal) | The project's going well vs. The project is progressing according to schedule."}},{"id":"vW0xY1zA2b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Hedging language is also vital in formal contexts to avoid overstating claims: The evidence suggests... / It appears that... / This may indicate... Overconfident assertions can undermine credibility in academic and professional writing."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I would be grateful if you could address this matter at your earliest convenience.

content.content: {"time":1700000012000,"blocks":[{"id":"cD3eF4gH5i","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A professional email has a predictable and expected structure. Deviating from this structure risks appearing unprofessional or creating confusion. The key components are: subject line, salutation, opening, body, closing, sign-off, and signature."}},{"id":"jK6lM7nO8p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Subject line: Precise and informative — Re: Meeting Rescheduled — 14 May rather than Meeting. Use title case and keep it under 60 characters."}},{"id":"qR9sT0uV1w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Salutation: When writing to someone you do not know well: Dear Mr. /Ms. [Surname]. When the recipient's name is unknown: Dear Sir or Madam."}},{"id":"xY2zA3bC4d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Opening sentence: State the purpose immediately. Preferred openings: I am writing to inform you that... / Further to our conversation last Tuesday, I would like to..."}},{"id":"eF5gH6iJ7k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Sign-off: Yours sincerely (when you know the recipient's name) | Yours faithfully (when you do not know the name) | Kind regards / Best regards (semi-formal, increasingly standard)."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I am writing with regard to your advertisement for the position of Senior Analyst.

pairs.right: Used when you know the recipient's name
Used when the name is unknown (Dear Sir/Madam)
Semi-formal, increasingly common in professional emails

[Further to] our telephone conversation on 12 April, I would like to [confirm] my attendance at the interview. Please [do not hesitate] to contact me if you require any [further] information. Yours [sincerely],

options: Yours sincerely
Kind regards
Yours faithfully

content.content: {"time":1700000013000,"blocks":[{"id":"lM8nO9pQ0r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Complaint and apology letters require careful management of tone. A complaint must be assertive without being aggressive; an apology must be sincere without being excessively self-deprecating."}},{"id":"sT1uV2wX3y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Complaint email structure: (1) State the problem clearly and factually. (2) Explain the impact or inconvenience caused. (3) State what you expect to be done. (4) Set a reasonable deadline if appropriate. Avoid emotional language: I was disappointed to find that... / I trust that this matter will be resolved promptly."}},{"id":"zA4bC5dE6f","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Apology email structure: (1) Acknowledge the problem without deflection. (2) Apologise sincerely. (3) Explain what happened. (4) State what corrective action has been or will be taken. Key phrases: I sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused. / We take full responsibility for this error."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

options: Your service was absolutely terrible.
I was extremely disappointed with the quality of the product I received.

lessons.title: Structure and Language of Business Reports

content.content: {"time":1700000014000,"blocks":[{"id":"gH7iJ8kL9m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A business report is a structured document that presents information, analysis, and (often) recommendations to a specific audience for a specific purpose. Unlike essays, reports use headings, numbered sections, and bullet points to aid navigation and clarity."}},{"id":"nO0pQ1rS2t","type":"header","data":{"text":"Standard report structure:","level":3}},{"id":"uV3wX4yZ5a","type":"list","data":{"style":"ordered","items":["Title page — title, author, date, addressee.","Executive summary — a brief overview.","Introduction — purpose, scope, methodology.","Findings — facts and analysis, usually with subheadings.","Conclusions — interpretation of findings.","Recommendations — specific, actionable proposals.","Appendices — supporting data."]}},{"id":"bC6dE7fG8h","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Language patterns specific to reports: describing purpose: The purpose of this report is to examine...; presenting findings: The data indicates that...; making recommendations: It is recommended that the company consider..."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: The purpose of this report is to examine the causes of declining customer satisfaction.

pairs.right: Brief overview of the entire report
Presentation and analysis of data collected
Specific, actionable proposals based on findings

content.text: The [purpose] of this report is to [examine] the causes of declining customer satisfaction. The data [indicates] that response times have increased by 40% over the past quarter. It is [recommended] that the customer service team [be expanded] and that training protocols [be reviewed].

questions.text: Which section of a business report contains specific, actionable proposals based on the findings?
options: Introduction
Executive Summary
Recommendations
Appendices

content.content: {"time":1700000015000,"blocks":[{"id":"iJ9kL0mN1o","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"An argumentative essay presents a position on a debatable topic and defends it with evidence and reasoning. At B2 level, the essay must demonstrate not just vocabulary and grammar, but the ability to organise ideas logically, acknowledge opposing views, and reach a well-supported conclusion."}},{"id":"pQ2rS3tU4v","type":"header","data":{"text":"Standard essay structure:","level":3}},{"id":"wX5yZ6aB7c","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Introduction — background context, thesis statement","Body paragraphs — each paragraph makes one point (topic sentence + evidence + explanation + link)","Counter-argument paragraph — acknowledge the opposing view and refute it","Conclusion — restate the thesis, summarise main points, give a final reflection"]}},{"id":"dE8fG9hI0j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Thesis statement is the backbone of the essay. Compare: Social media is bad (too vague) vs. While social media facilitates global connection, its role in amplifying misinformation poses a significant threat to democratic discourse (specific and arguable)."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: While social media facilitates global connection, its role in amplifying misinformation poses a significant threat to democratic discourse.

lessons.title: Writing Concise and Effective Executive Summaries

content.content: {"time":1700000016000,"blocks":[{"id":"kL1mN2oP3q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"An executive summary is a condensed version of a longer document — typically a report, proposal, or research study — designed for busy decision-makers who may not read the full document. It must be self-contained: a reader who reads only the summary should understand the key issue, findings, and recommended actions."}},{"id":"rS4tU5vW6x","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Length: Typically 10–15% of the full document, or 1–2 pages for a 10–15 page report."}},{"id":"yZ7aB8cD9e","type":"header","data":{"text":"Key components:","level":3}},{"id":"fG0hI1jK2l","type":"list","data":{"style":"ordered","items":["Background/Purpose — Why was this report produced?","Key Findings — The most significant data and analysis.","Conclusions — What do the findings mean?","Recommendations — What actions should be taken?"]}},{"id":"mN3oP4qR5s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Language: Concise, direct, and active where possible: Sales declined by 12% in Q3 (not There was a decline in the area of sales performance). Use bullet points for recommendations."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

options: To provide a detailed analysis of all findings
To allow busy readers to grasp the key points without reading the full document
To introduce new data not covered in the main report
To replace the introduction section of a report

options: There were some issues identified in the area of customer service delivery.

lessons.title: Writing a Professional CV and Cover Letter

content.content: {"time":1700000017000,"blocks":[{"id":"tU6vW7xY8z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A CV (Curriculum Vitae) is a structured document presenting your education, professional experience, skills, and achievements. In English-speaking professional contexts, it should be concise, consistent, and tailored to the specific role you are applying for."}},{"id":"aB9cD0eF1g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"CV principles: Use action verbs in the past tense for previous roles: Managed a team of 12 analysts / Coordinate cross-departmental projects. Quantify achievements where possible: Increased sales revenue by 35% within 18 months is far more compelling than Improved sales."}},{"id":"hI2jK3lM4n","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Cover letter should not simply repeat your CV — it should interpret your experience for the reader. Avoid clichés: I am a hard-working team player with a passion for... Instead, demonstrate your qualities through specific evidence: During my three years at X, I led a team that delivered Y, resulting in Z."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

lessons.title: Linking Ideas: Discourse Markers and Cohesive Devices

content.content: {"time":1700000018000,"blocks":[{"id":"oP5qR6sT7u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Cohesion refers to the grammatical and lexical links within and between sentences that create a unified text. Coherence refers to the logical flow of ideas. Strong professional writing achieves both."}},{"id":"vW8xY9zA0b","type":"header","data":{"text":"Discourse markers by function:","level":3}},{"id":"cD1eF2gH3i","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Addition: Furthermore, Moreover, In addition, What is more","Contrast: However, Nevertheless, Nonetheless, In contrast, Notwithstanding","Cause/result: Consequently, Therefore, As a result, Hence, Thus","Concession: Admittedly, While it is true that, Despite this, Even so","Exemplification: For instance, For example, To illustrate, Such as","Conclusion: In conclusion, To summarise, On balance, Taking everything into account"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}
